claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity relative to a random solid solution in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
Boundaries of SRO domains enhance phonon scattering.
SRO disrupts phonon coherence.
The initial random solid solution in a refractory HEA is characterized by severe lattice distortion.
Annealing MoNbTaW near 800 K can induce an SRO state.
SRO in the proposed refractory alloy may adopt L12- or L11-type local arrangements.
Lattice thermal conductivity dominates heat transport in refractory HEAs from cryogenic temperatures to approximately 1500 K.
SRO produces diffuse antiphase boundaries in MoNbTaW.
SRO-domain interfaces scatter phonons because of local variations in atomic mass, bond stiffness, and lattice strain.
The relevant SRO domains have a characteristic size of approximately 1–2 nm.
Atomic-scale mass-variance scattering is present in both the RSS and SRO states.
SRO creates a hierarchical scattering landscape by adding domain-interface scattering to atomic-scale disorder scattering.
Vibrational mismatch across SRO boundaries preferentially scatters mid- to long-wavelength phonons.
Additional scattering at SRO boundaries reduces the phonon mean free path.
SRO enhances edge-dislocation mobility in MoNbTaW.
The SRO alloy will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than the RSS counterpart from approximately 300 K to 1500 K.
Thermal-conductivity suppression is greatest when the phonon mean free path is comparable to the SRO-domain size.
Diffuse superlattice reflections can arise from diffuse scattering across SRO domains.
Long-range ordering with coherent domains larger than the phonon mean free path may reduce phonon scattering.
Changes in SRO character or SRO parameter with temperature can produce non-monotonic thermal-transport behavior.
